title: Rigveda 5.76: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.76: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.76 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 391v-392r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.76.1-2 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 391v
translation.original_text:
1ā bhā̍ty a̱gnir u̱ṣasā̱m anī̍ka̱m ud viprā̍ṇāṁ deva̱yā vāco̍ asthuḥ | a̱rvāñcā̍ nū̱naṁ ra̍thye̱ha yā̍tam pīpi̱vāṁsa̍m aśvinā gha̱rmam accha̍ ||
2na sa̍ṁskṛ̱tam pra mi̍mīto̱ gami̱ṣṭhānti̍ nū̱nam a̱śvinopa̍stute̱ha | divā̍bhipi̱tve 'va̱sāga̍miṣṭhā̱ praty ava̍rtiṁ dā̱śuṣe̱ śambha̍viṣṭhā ||
translation.text:
1AGNI, the bright face of the Dawns, is shining; the singers' pious voices have ascended. Borne on your chariot, Aṣvins, turn you hither and come unto our full and rich libation.
2Most frequent guests, they scorn not what is ready: even now the lauded Aṣvins are beside us. With promptest aid they come at morn and evening, the worshipper's most blessed guards from trouble.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 391v (numbered 64v by the scribe) (OPenn image 392, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.75.7 ‹yātam adābhyā mādhvī iti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 392r (numbered 65r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.76.3 ‹ā yātam sam-gave prātaḥ›. Verses 5.76.1-2 end on this page.

2na | saṃskṛtam | pra | mimītaḥ | gamiṣṭhā | anti | nūnam | aśvinā | upa-stutā | iha | divā | abhi-pitve | avasā | āgamiṣṭhā | prati | avartim | dāśuṣe | śam-bhaviṣṭhā

translation.original_ref: RV 5.76.3-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 392r
translation.original_text:
3u̱tā yā̍taṁ saṁga̱ve prā̱tar ahno̍ ma̱dhyaṁdi̍na̱ udi̍tā̱ sūrya̍sya | divā̱ nakta̱m ava̍sā̱ śaṁta̍mena̱ nedānī̍m pī̱tir a̱śvinā ta̍tāna ||
4i̱daṁ hi vā̍m pra̱divi̱ sthāna̱m oka̍ i̱me gṛ̱hā a̍śvine̱daṁ du̍ro̱ṇam | ā no̍ di̱vo bṛ̍ha̱taḥ parva̍tā̱d ādbhyo yā̍ta̱m iṣa̱m ūrja̱ṁ vaha̍ntā ||
5sam a̱śvino̱r ava̍sā̱ nūta̍nena mayo̱bhuvā̍ su̱praṇī̍tī gamema | ā no̍ ra̱yiṁ va̍hata̱m ota vī̱rān ā viśvā̍ny amṛtā̱ saubha̍gāni ||
translation.text:
3Yea, come at milking-time, at early morning, at noon of day and when the Sun is setting, By day, by night, with favour most auspicious. Not only now the draught hath drawn the Aṣvins.
4For this place, Aṣvins, was of old your dwelling, these were your houses, this your habitation. Come to us from high heaven and from the mountain. Come from the waters bringing food and vigour.
5May we obtain the Aṣvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance. Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 392r (numbered 65r by the scribe) (OPenn image 392, lower leaf). The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 392v (numbered 65v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.77.2 ‹-yajamānaḥ vanīyān›. Verses 5.76.3-5 end on this page; 5.76.3 begins on fol. 391v (numbered 64v by the scribe).
